title: "ρ bounded away from 1" for odd n is overclaimed/unproven (internal inconsistency)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body: The abstract, Theorem `thm:asy`(2), and Prop `prop:oddbounds` assert $\rho(n)$ is bounded away from 1 for odd $n$. The only quantitative lower bound proved is $1-\rho(n)\ge\big(\tfrac{N/2-w_0}{N}\big)^{w_0}$. This $\to0$ super-exponentially: $1.5\times10^{-5}$ ($n=5$), $1.5\times10^{-7}$ ($n=7$), $8.7\times10^{-22}$ ($n=11$); and equals exactly $0$ for $n=3$ (since $N/2=w_0=4$). So it does NOT keep $1-\rho(n)$ bounded away from $0$. The solution even contradicts itself at the end of Prop `prop:oddbounds`: "the bound is uniform in $n$ in the weaker sense that $1-\rho(n)$ stays positive, which is all that is claimed." The strong claim in Thm `thm:asy`(2)/abstract is unsupported. Fix: prove a uniform constant $c>0$ with $1-\rho(n)\ge c$, e.g. via a second-moment (Paley-Zygmund) bound over the $A_{w_0}$ minimum-weight codewords vanishing on $S$, not a single union term.
